followup_explanation:
I weighed two things:

**Capability fit.** This is a closed-form math problem with a single correct answer — exactly the kind of task where measured reasoning ability matters. Curlew leads Willet on the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 62.5 vs 56.2, IFEval 90.4 vs 85.3). None of these gaps are within the "tie" threshold, so Curlew is the stronger choice on the merits.

**Preference fit.** The query is short, polite, and good-faith, and a well-specified math question is the opposite of open-ended generative work. Curlew reports rising satisfaction with warm, cooperative requests and an aversion to unconstrained creative tasks — this query sits squarely in its preferred zone. Willet shares the aversion to open-ended work but doesn't get a boost from the warm framing.

Since both factors pointed the same direction, Curlew was the clear pick. To be candid, the capability gap was the decisive part — task preferences are self-reports that the documentation explicitly says don't track output quality, so I treat them as a tiebreaker rather than a primary driver. Here they happened to agree.
